purpose: Alitretinoin is used to treat severe chronic hand eczema that has not responded to other treatments. It is also used as a gel to treat skin sores caused by Kaposi's sarcoma, a type of cancer related to HIV/AIDS. Your doctor will decide which form is right for your condition.
how_it_works: Alitretinoin is related to Vitamin A and works by binding to special receptors in your skin cells. This helps regulate how skin cells grow and reduces inflammation. In Kaposi's sarcoma, it also helps slow the growth of abnormal cancer cells in the skin.
common_side_effects: Headaches, dry skin, lips, and eyes, redness or peeling of the skin, increased sensitivity to sunlight, joint or muscle aches, and elevated cholesterol or triglyceride levels in your blood. The gel form may cause local skin irritation, redness, or rash at the application site.
warnings: This medication must NEVER be taken if you are pregnant or could become pregnant — it causes serious birth defects. You must use reliable contraception before, during, and after treatment. Do not donate blood while taking it. Avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen daily. Regular blood tests are needed to monitor cholesterol, liver, and thyroid levels. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially vitamin A supplements.
typical_dosing: For capsules (hand eczema): The usual starting dose is 30 mg taken by mouth once a day with a main meal. Your doctor may adjust to 10 mg or 30 mg based on how you respond and any side effects. For the gel (Kaposi's sarcoma): Apply a thin layer directly to the skin sore 2 to 4 times daily as directed by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
